subject: general
question: According to Article 130 of the Constitution of India, the Supreme Court shall sit in Delhi or in such other place or places as may be appointed by:

options.text: the President, in consultation with the Prime Minister
the Union Cabinet, with advice from the Law Ministry
the Chief Justice of India, with the approval of the President

solution:
The correct answer is __**the Chief Justice of India, with the approval of the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per **Article 130** of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court shall sit in Delhi or such other place or places as the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**, with the approval of the President, may appoint.
 
• This provision grants the Chief Justice of India the authority to decide on the location of the Supreme Court’s sittings, subject to Presidential approval.
 
• The Constitution originally envisaged the Supreme Court to be located in Delhi, but Article 130 allows flexibility for the Court to sit in other parts of the country if necessary.
 
• The provision ensures that the Supreme Court is accessible to people across India, facilitating better access to justice.
 
• Such relocation of sittings, however, has not been exercised so far, and the Supreme Court primarily operates from its premises in New Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court (Composition & Appointment):**

 
 
• Judges: Chief Justice of India (CJI) + up to 33 other Judges (total 34).
 
• Appointment: Appointed by the President, with significant consultation from the Collegium (CJI & senior judges).
 
• Tenure: Judges retire at 65 years of age.
 
• Removal: Only by Parliament through a rigorous impeachment process for proven misbehavior or incapacity.
